example.scenario: MITM Wi-Fi Eavesdropping on Unsecured Public Network Captures HTTP Basic Auth Credentials

packet_capture_excerpt: Frame 45: 1514 bytes on wire (12112 bits), 1514 bytes captured (12112 bits)
Transmission Control Protocol, Src Port: 51234, Dst Port: 80, Seq: 1, Ack: 1, Len: 1460

indicators: Presence of HTTP Authorization header with Basic auth base64 encoded credentials in plaintext
Unencrypted HTTP traffic over Wi-Fi network with SSID 'FreePublicWiFi' and no encryption
ARP spoofing activity seen in network (arpspoof running with target IP 192.168.1.101)
TCP connections on port 80 with captured Authorization headers
MITM proxy logs showing intercepted credentials
example.detection_method: Network IDS/IPS detecting ARP spoofing attempts with frequent gratuitous ARP packets, monitoring for HTTP Basic Auth headers in traffic over unsecured Wi-Fi networks, endpoint detection for unauthorized MITM proxy processes, and alerting on plaintext credential exposure.

example.scenario: MITM Attack Captures Session Cookies Over WPA2 Enterprise Network Due to Rogue Access Point

technical_data.tcpdump_filter_command: tcpdump -i wlan0 -nn -s 0 -w mitm_capture.pcap tcp port 80 or tcp port 443
mitmproxy_intercepted_https_traffic: ServerHello intercepted, SSL certificate replaced by rogue AP's self-signed certificate
Decrypted HTTPS traffic showing session cookie: sessionid=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
technical_data.openssl_verification_failure:
openssl s_client -connect internal.corp.example.com:443
Verify return code: 18 (self signed certificate)

indicators: Duplicate SSID 'CorpWiFi' with conflicting security settings (WPA2-Enterprise vs open)
Unusual DHCP server offering IP addresses on corporate VLAN but with unexpected MAC (00:11:22:33:44:55)
Self-signed SSL certificates presented for legitimate corporate domains
Captured HTTP/HTTPS traffic with session cookies in plaintext or decrypted via rogue AP
User complaints of certificate warnings or connection errors when connecting to corporate Wi-Fi
example.detection_method: Wireless network monitoring for rogue APs broadcasting duplicate SSIDs, certificate pinning on clients to detect invalid certificates, DHCP server monitoring for unauthorized servers, and IDS signatures for SSL MITM attacks with certificate anomalies.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols

The technical data is comprehensive, including Wi-Fi scan results showing conflicting security settings, DHCP offers from the rogue AP, captured HTTP and decrypted HTTPS traffic with session cookies, and evidence of SSL interception via self-signed certificates. The indicators clearly explain why this is a MITM attack involving Wi-Fi eavesdropping, highlighting duplicate SSIDs, rogue DHCP servers, certificate anomalies, and captured sensitive data. example.scenario: MITM Attack Using Evil Twin Wi-Fi AP to Capture OAuth Tokens via Unencrypted Redirects
indicators: Open Wi-Fi network broadcasting legitimate SSID 'CoffeeShop_WiFi' but with different BSSID and channel than known good AP
HTTP 302 redirects to attacker-controlled domain from OAuth provider domain
Captured OAuth access tokens in HTTP GET fragment parameters sent to attacker-controlled server
DNS spoofing rules redirecting oauth-provider.com to local attacker IP
Use of mitmproxy or similar intercepting and modifying OAuth authentication flows
example.detection_method: Wireless network fingerprinting to detect rogue AP BSSID mismatches, network traffic analysis for OAuth token leakage in unencrypted HTTP redirects, DNS query anomaly detection, and monitoring client endpoint logs for unexpected OAuth token transmissions.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1557.001 - Man-in-the-Middle: ARP Spoofing (used for DNS spoofing)
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
